sections.overview: Lahaul & Spiti is the largest and most remote district of Himachal Pradesh — a high-altitude cold desert averaging 4,000 m. Accessible via Rohtang Pass (from Manali) or Kinnaur route. The Spiti Valley contains some of the world's oldest Buddhist monasteries: Key, Tabo (1,000 years old), Dhankar. The landscape is stark, lunar and striking. Chandratal lake is one of India's most photographed Himalayan lakes.

chandratal_lake.description: Translated as 'Moon Lake', Chandratal sits at 4,250 m in a glacial bowl near the Kunzum Pass, its crescent shape giving it its name when viewed from the ridges above. The water is an extraordinary deep blue-green, reflecting the surrounding moraines and the snow peak of Chandra Bhaga in extraordinary clarity at dawn before the winds arrive. Camping is permitted 500 m from the lake shore (no camping on the lake margin); the site has basic toilet facilities and a small dhaba that operates in season. The approach road from Batal, 14 km on a rough track, is passable in 4WD vehicles from June to early October. The lake is considered sacred by Buddhists, and legend holds that fairies come to bathe here on moonlit nights.
chandratal_lake.name: Chandratal Lake

dhankar.description: The medieval village of Dhankar clings to a near-vertical cliff face at the confluence of the Spiti and Pin rivers, its 1,000-year-old monastery and crumbling fort seemingly defying gravity above a 1,000 m drop to the valley floor. The 4th-century fort ruins above the monastery hold copper-age inscriptions and command among the most dramatic viewpoints in the Spiti Valley. A 1-hour trail from the village leads to the Dhankar Lake — a small glacial tarn at 4,100 m surrounded by rough moraines. The monastery itself, though structurally fragile, contains important murals and hosts a small resident community of monks. Dhankar receives a fraction of the visitors that Key does, preserving a palpable sense of solitude.
dhankar.name: Dhankar

hikkim.description: At 4,400 m on the plateau above Kaza, Hikkim holds the distinction of being home to the world's highest functioning post office — a small white building where travellers queue to send postcards stamped with the coveted 'Hikkim' postmark that collectors prize. The village of a few dozen houses grows peas and barley in the short growing season and is inhabited throughout the year by families who winter at lower elevations. The plateau walk from Hikkim to Komic village (one of the world's highest motorable villages) across open tundra, with views to the Kinnaur Kailash range, is a notable short walks in Spiti. The clarity of night sky here, far from any light pollution, makes Hikkim exceptional for astrophotography.
hikkim.name: Hikkim

kaza.description: At 3,800 m in the Spiti river valley, Kaza is the administrative and logistical hub of Spiti sub-division — a compact town of whitewashed government buildings, a busy market street and a growing number of guesthouses and cafes that cater to the summer influx of motorcyclists and trekkers. The New Kaza market area has ATMs, a petrol pump, medical centre and mobile data connectivity (BSNL), making it a critical resupply point before heading to the higher villages. The old Kaza fort ruins on the ridge above town offer views down the valley to the confluence of the Pin and Spiti rivers. Most visitors use Kaza as a 2–3 night base from which to explore Key, Kibber, Langza, Hikkim and the Pin Valley.
kaza.name: Kaza

key_monastery.description: Perched on a conical hill at 4,166 m above the Spiti river, Ki (Key) Gompa is the largest and most visited monastery in the Spiti Valley — a white-washed labyrinth of prayer halls, monks' quarters and meditation rooms that has expanded organically over 1,000 years. The oldest sections date to the 11th century, and the monastery was damaged repeatedly by Mongol raids, earthquakes and fire before its current form was consolidated. Inside, ancient thangka paintings, butter sculptures and ritual objects fill the dimly lit shrines. The summer festival (June–July) brings the monastery alive with masked cham dances performed by resident monks. Resident monk numbers fluctuate between 250 and 300, and the monastery runs a school for young monks.
key_monastery.name: Key Monastery

langza.description: At 4,400 m on the same plateau as Hikkim, Langza is distinguished by a giant white Buddha statue overlooking the village and valley — and by an extraordinary geological phenomenon: the surrounding hillsides are rich in marine fossils, ammonites and trilobites preserved in the ancient Tethys Sea sediments that now form these Himalayan heights. Local children sell fossils to visitors; removing geological specimens is technically prohibited, though the trade persists. The village commands an unobstructed view of the Chau Chau Kang Nilda peak (6,303 m). The combined Langza–Hikkim–Komic plateau circuit (half-day by vehicle, full-day on foot) ranks among the most rewarding excursions from Kaza.
langza.name: Langza

pin_valley_national_park.description: Covering 675 sq km of the Pin river watershed at altitudes between 3,500 m and 6,600 m, Pin Valley National Park is one of India's highest protected areas and one of the best places in the world to sight snow leopards in their natural habitat. The park protects a transition zone between the moist alpine meadows of the Greater Himalaya and the cold desert of the Tibetan plateau — a habitat mosaic that supports snow leopard, Himalayan wolf, Tibetan wild ass (kiang), Himalayan ibex and over 100 bird species. The main valley road from Attargo to Mud village (4,050 m) passes through the park; the inner areas require a wildlife department permit and a registered guide. Winter (November–March) is the best season for snow leopard sightings when prey ibex descend to lower elevations.
pin_valley_national_park.name: Pin Valley National Park

rohtang_pass.description: The Rohtang Pass (4,111 m) functions as the great gateway of Lahaul — the point at which the monsoon-fed green world of the Kullu Valley abruptly gives way to the rain-shadow landscapes of Lahaul and ultimately Spiti. For Lahaul, Rohtang is not a visitor attraction but a lifeline: the pass closes from November to May under heavy snowfall, cutting Lahaul off from Manali and the outside world until the Atal Tunnel (opened 2020) changed the equation throughout the year. The approach from the Lahaul (northern) side is gentler than the Kullu face, passing the Chandra river headwaters and the vast flat Lahaul valley dotted with poplar trees and whitewashed gompas. The Atal Rohtang Tunnel at 3,100 m is now the practical route; the pass itself is visited as an excursion from Manali.
rohtang_pass.name: Rohtang Pass

sissu.description: In the green Lahaul valley just 5 km north of the Rohtang Tunnel's northern portal, Sissu is a revelation after the stark landscapes further north — a village of emerald fields, poplar windbreaks and apple orchards backed by a hanging glacier that sends a spectacular waterfall down a basalt cliff face into the Chandra river below. The flat valley floor here is good cycling territory, and the village guesthouses offer the most comfortable accommodation between Manali and Kaza. The Gemur monastery, a 12th-century Tibetan Buddhist site, sits above the village on a pine-forested slope. Sissu has become increasingly popular as a weekend destination from Manali since the Rohtang Tunnel opened.
sissu.name: Sissu

tabo_monastery.description: Founded in 996 CE by the Tibetan Buddhist scholar Rinchen Zangpo, Tabo is the oldest continuously functioning monastery in the Himalayan region and among the most remarkable surviving examples of medieval Buddhist art anywhere in Asia. The main Dukhang (assembly hall) and nine other temples contain exquisitely preserved 10th–12th century mud-plaster murals, clay sculptures and stucco figures in a style that bridges the Kashmiri and Central Asian traditions. The Dalai Lama has expressed a wish to retire here. Tabo village, at 3,050 m on the banks of the Spiti river, is quieter and warmer than Kaza, making it an ideal overnight stay before or after visiting Chandratal via the Pin Valley.
tabo_monastery.name: Tabo Monastery

sections.overview: Una is Himachal's gateway from Punjab, the flattest and hottest district in the state. This place is primarily a pilgrimage district — Chintpurni temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and receives millions of devotees annually. The Amb temples are early medieval stone temples in excellent condition. The Swan river flows through Una and now includes for light ecotourism. Una is also HP's industrial base (Baddi-Nalagarh industrial area partly falls here).

amb_temples.description: The Amb temple complex, 20 km from Una town near the village of Amb, is a group of early medieval Hindu temples dating to the 8th–9th century in the Pratihara style — remarkable because they are among the finest and best-preserved ancient stone temples in the outer Himalayan belt, and yet virtually unknown outside academic circles. The main shikhara temples, built in the nagara (north Indian) style with carved exteriors depicting Vishnu, Shiva and their attendants, are protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. The site is set in agricultural land with a pleasant rural character. The quality of the stone carving — particularly the doorway guardians and the river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna — is comparable to more famous temple sites of the period.
amb_temples.name: Amb Temples

bangana_craft_village.description: A rural cluster in the border zone between Una and Hamirpur districts, Bangana and its surrounding villages are known for traditional Himachali textile weaving — particularly the production of heavy wool pattus (shawls) and blankets using horizontal frame looms that are still operated in domestic settings. A Himachal Pradesh government crafts development initiative has supported a small weavers' cooperative that welcomes visitors and sells directly. The weaving process — carding, spinning and slow shuttle weaving — can be observed in family homes with advance notice through the cooperative. The products, particularly the heavy natural-dyed blankets, are significantly cheaper here than in urban craft emporiums.
bangana_craft_village.name: Bangana Craft Village

chintpurni_temple.description: The Chintpurni Devi temple at 920 m in the Shivalik foothills is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas — sacred sites associated with the body of the goddess Sati — and is among the most heavily visited religious sites in Himachal Pradesh, receiving an estimated 7–10 million pilgrims annually from Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Jammu. The goddess Chinnamastika, the headless form of Durga, is venerated here with particular intensity during the Navratri festivals (March–April and September–October). The approach road from Una (52 km) through the Shivalik forest is now well-maintained. Enormous prasad preparations — particularly kheer and halwa — and the constant flow of devotional music give the temple precinct a vibrantly intense devotional atmosphere.
chintpurni_temple.name: Chintpurni Temple

dera_baba_rudra_nand.description: The ashram of the Shaivite saint Baba Rudra Nand on the outskirts of Una town is an active spiritual centre in the Nath tradition — the ancient yogic lineage associated with Guru Gorakhnath. The ashram conducts regular satsang (spiritual gatherings), yoga classes and meditation programmes that are open to visitors. The main temple is an attractive structure set in planted gardens. The ashram also maintains a charitable school and health clinic serving surrounding villages. Visitors are welcome with appropriate respect for the spiritual atmosphere; the institution maintains a simple, non-commercial character despite its proximity to the busy Una town.
dera_baba_rudra_nand.name: Dera Baba Rudra Nand

kutlehar_fort.description: The ruined fort of the former Kutlehar princely state — one of the 30+ small principalities that dotted the Shivalik foothills before independence — stands on a forested hillside above the Una valley, its stone walls and corner bastions now largely consumed by vegetation. The Kutlehar state, which managed to maintain autonomy through the British period, acceded to India in 1948; its former palace in the village below has been converted to private use. The climb to the fort summit through secondary forest takes approximately 30 minutes and offers views over the Una valley floor and the Swan river floodplain. The site is not formally developed for tourism and is visited primarily by local history enthusiasts.
kutlehar_fort.name: Kutlehar Fort

nangal_dam.description: The Nangal Dam on the Satluj river, just south of the HP-Punjab border near Nangal town, is the downstream component of the Bhakra-Nangal project — India's largest post-Independence irrigation and hydro project, inaugurated by Nehru in 1963. The Nangal reservoir stretches back toward Bilaspur and forms the lower basin of Gobind Sagar. The dam structure itself, significantly smaller than the Bhakra main dam, can be visited with security clearance; the township built for project engineers retains its planned 1950s character. The reservoir margins on the HP side have good birdlife, particularly in winter when the Bhakra-Nangal reservoir system attracts bar-headed geese, Eurasian wigeons and various diving ducks.
nangal_dam.name: Nangal Dam

pong_dam_wildlife_sanctuary.description: The 307 sq km Pong Dam Wetland, created by the impounding of the Beas river at Pong on the HP-Punjab border, is a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance and among the most significant waterfowl wintering grounds in the western Himalaya. The reservoir, at its peak in November–February, hosts up to 100,000 bar-headed geese — a single population of this high-altitude migratory species that breeds on the Tibetan plateau and winters here. Over 220 species of waterbirds have been recorded including greylag goose, common crane, tufted duck, ferruginous duck and various tern species. The Wildlife Department maintains boat-based viewing safaris from the Nagrota Surian entry point on the HP shore. Winter mornings when the geese lift off the water in enormous flocks are among the great wildlife spectacles of northern India.
pong_dam_wildlife_sanctuary.name: Pong Dam Wildlife Sanctuary

sathali_devi_temple.description: A small but ancient goddess temple on a forested ridge 6 km from Chintpurni, Sathali Devi is venerated as a complementary deity to the Chintpurni goddess — many pilgrims to Chintpurni include Sathali in their circuit. The ridge on which the temple sits offers views over the Shivalik foothills and the Una valley that are particularly scenic in the early morning light. The surrounding deodar forest, relatively intact because of the religious protection of the temple catchment, supports good woodland birdlife. The temple is tended by a hereditary priest family from the adjacent village.
sathali_devi_temple.name: Sathali Devi Temple

swan_river_eco_park.description: The Swan river, a seasonal flashflood-prone stream draining the Shivalik foothills into the Punjab plains, now includes in Una into a linear riverside park where channelisation work and bank planting have created a green corridor through the town. The eco park section, stretching approximately 3 km, has walking and cycling paths, bird observation points and seasonal gardens. In winter (November–February) the river's edge attracts migratory birds including various egret species, kingfishers and lapwings. The park is a popular local amenity for Una town residents and a pleasant space for early morning walks in the cooler months.
swan_river_eco_park.name: Swan River Eco Park

una_town.description: The district headquarters of Una at 369 m is the flattest and warmest point in Himachal Pradesh — a commercial and administrative centre in the foothills that serves as the main entry point into the state from Punjab. The Swan river, channelised through the town, now includes into a linear river park with walking paths and gardens. The Una railway station on the Pathankot-Una Himachal Railway line connects the district directly to the Punjab rail network. Una's industrial character, dominated by the pharmaceutical factories of the Mehatpur and Bharwain industrial estates, gives it a distinctly different atmosphere from the mountain districts of Himachal.
una_town.name: Una Town
